IDA credit for early childhood education and women’s jobs, approval announced 20 April 2026: 60 new preschool classrooms and around 80 early development centres

register.name: Belize Early Childhood Development and Female Empowerment Project
register.detail: World Bank Board approval announced 20 April 2026 · IDA credit · with a US$1.28 million Early Learning Partnership grant
register.note: 60 new preschool classrooms, 30 preschools upgraded and around 80 early development centres
register.text: An IDA credit, with a grant from the Early Learning Partnership, to widen access to quality, inclusive early childhood education and to help women into work. It adds 60 classrooms to primary schools in communities without preschools, rehabilitates or upgrades 30 preschools and establishes or upgrades around 80 early development centres for children up to age 4. It serves education, the standard furthest from reach in Belize, and livelihood.

register.name: Scaling up early warning services (CREWS) in Belize and Trinidad and Tobago (SAP063)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved 30 October 2025 · GCF grant USD 24,117,448 · accredited entity: Caribbean Development Bank · CDB release of 7 August 2026
register.note: US$27.1 million for Belize and Trinidad and Tobago together; no share for Belize is stated
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, channelled through the Caribbean Development Bank, to scale up hydrometeorological services and multi-hazard early warning systems in Belize and Trinidad and Tobago, with the Caribbean Meteorological Organisation and the national meteorological and disaster management agencies. It strengthens the forecasting and timely warnings that protect homes, harvests and livelihoods.

register.name: Integrated Utility Services (IUS) for the Caribbean, Phase 1 (FP275)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved 3 July 2025 · GCF loan US$20.8 million and grant US$5.9 million · accredited entity: Caribbean Development Bank · six years
register.note: US$26.7 million of GCF financing for Barbados, Belize and Jamaica together; no share for Belize is stated
register.text: A six-year Green Climate Fund programme, through the Caribbean Development Bank, to accelerate distributed renewable energy, energy efficiency and other clean energy technologies, including rooftop solar, in Barbados, Belize and Jamaica. The CDB expects it to benefit 40,700 people across the three nations; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Rural Electrification Program
register.detail: IDB · approved 16 September 2026 · US$20 million loan, 25 years with five and a half years’ grace · US$2.75 million and US$1 million in non-reimbursable financing
register.note: About 3,000 rural households to be connected
register.text: An IDB package of a US$20 million loan and US$3.75 million of non-reimbursable financing to bring electricity to about 3,000 rural households, in communities with a high share of Indigenous peoples and migrants. It pays for solar photovoltaic minigrids with battery storage, smart metering and extensions of the distribution grid. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Catastrophe swap for hurricane risk
register.detail: IDB, with Swiss Re providing the parametric coverage · protection from 1 August 2026 to 31 May 2028 · maximum payout US$10 million per policy year · the first of its kind at the IDB
register.note: Up to US$20 million of coverage; the Government of Belize contributes to the premium
register.text: An IDB catastrophe swap that transfers part of Belize’s hurricane risk to the reinsurance market through Swiss Re, which provides the underlying parametric coverage. Funds are released when pre-agreed hurricane triggers are met, protecting the public finances behind the seven standards against hurricane losses.

register.name: Basic Needs Trust Fund, eleventh programme (BNTF 11)
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · launched in Belize City, release of 15 July 2026 · with the Belize Social Investment Fund · four-year cycle
register.note: More than US$5.2 million for six sub-projects: four in education, two in water
register.text: The Caribbean Development Bank’s community programme, launched in Belize with the Government and the Belize Social Investment Fund. Belize’s allocation of more than US$5.2 million funds six sub-projects, four in education and two in water, over a four-year cycle. It serves education, the standard furthest from reach, and water.

register.name: Public-sector efficiency loan
register.detail: IDB Board of Executive Directors · executed by the Ministry of Public Service and Disaster Risk Management · five-year disbursement period · total cost US$9 million, with US$1 million of local counterpart funding
register.note: An integrated human resources information system, payroll controls, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity
register.text: An IDB loan of up to US$8 million to make the public service more efficient: an integrated Human Resources Management Information System, stronger payroll controls, workforce planning and compensation reforms, and investment in digital infrastructure, data management and cybersecurity. It strengthens the public administration that delivers the services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Eighth Power Project, Belize Electricity Limited
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · approved in 2025 · grid modernisation for about 114,000 households and businesses
register.note: Part of US$464 million of new support the CDB approved in 2025
register.text: Caribbean Development Bank financing for Belize’s Eighth Power Project, to modernise the electricity grid for about 114,000 households and businesses. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Labour force participation and employability programme
register.detail: IDB · loan contract signed · US$7 million loan with a five-and-a-half-year grace period · US$1 million from the IDB Grant Facility · a separate US$7 million loan from Taiwan’s ICDF
register.note: Over 20,000 jobseekers, including at least 2,360 trained in priority sectors
register.text: An IDB package of a US$7 million loan and US$1 million of non-reimbursable financing to modernise public employment services, with digital platforms for job matching, labour market information and case management, and training in high-demand sectors such as tourism. It is expected to serve over 20,000 jobseekers and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Skills for the Future Program
register.detail: IDB loan US$15 million, 25 years with five and a half years’ grace · Global Partnership for Education grant US$5 million
register.note: Six high schools to become STEAM labs; a third of secondary students to benefit
register.text: A US$20 million programme approved by the IDB and the Global Partnership for Education for foundational learning, workforce skills, gender gaps and inclusive education at primary and secondary level, including technical and vocational training. Low-performing students in all government-financed primary schools can take part. It serves education, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Sustainable and Inclusive Belize (BL-L1041)
register.detail: IDB · approved 14 September 2022 · in implementation · agriculture and tourism
register.note: Competitiveness, climate resilience and environmental sustainability of small businesses
register.text: An IDB loan to improve incomes and promote sustainable livelihoods in the agriculture and tourism sectors, by improving the competitiveness, climate resilience and environmental sustainability of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Blue Bond for Ocean Conservation
register.detail: The Nature Conservancy · Credit Suisse · US DFC political risk insurance · financial close November 2021
register.text: A blue loan through The Nature Conservancy refinanced the $553 million Superbond; Belize committed to protect 30% of its ocean.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity generated from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Nine tenths of the electricity generated at home is renewable, while half of the electricity used is imported.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 26.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Hillside Health Care International
items.text: A faith-based non-profit near Eldridgeville in the Toledo District, working in Belize since 2000, that gives free primary care at its outpatient clinic and on mobile clinics to 16 villages, with about 50 patients visited at home each week. It earns income by hosting medical students on four-week rotations.

items.name: Maya Mountain Cacao
items.text: A certified B Corp that operates on a social enterprise model, buying fresh cacao beans from more than 500 smallholder farmers in southern Belize, processing them at a central facility and facilitating organic certification for participating farms (2025).

items.name: Trio Farmers Cacao Growers
items.text: A company of 31 mostly Indigenous Maya farmers from Trio that runs a 379-hectare agroforestry concession in the Maya Mountain North Forest Reserve; in 2024 it reaped a record harvest of 63.5 tonnes of wet cacao beans.
